description: This bar chart illustrates the Module Giga FLOPs consumed by four different attention mechanisms—grouped attention (g=3), patch attention (k=3), and feed-forward—as well as a baseline (represented by the blue bar, which is unlabeled in the legend but appears to be a reference or default configuration)—across three stages of an audio back-end Conformer architecture. The horizontal axis categorizes the data by stage: Stage 1 (d=180, n=500), Stage 2 (d=256, n=250), and Stage 3 (d=360, n=125), with the parameters d and n likely representing dimensionality and sequence length respectively. The vertical axis measures Module Giga FLOPs on a linear scale ranging from 0 to 0.3, with major gridlines and tick marks at intervals of 0.1. For each stage, four bars are grouped side-by-side: the blue bar (unlabeled in legend) is consistently the tallest, followed by the red bar (grouped attention), then the green bar (feed-forward), and finally the yellow bar (patch attention), which is consistently the shortest. In Stage 1, the blue bar reaches approximately 0.28 Giga FLOPs, the red bar is at approximately 0.15 Giga FLOPs, the green bar is at approximately 0.12 Giga FLOPs, and the yellow bar is at approximately 0.11 Giga FLOPs. In Stage 2, the blue bar is at approximately 0.16 Giga FLOPs, the red bar is at approximately 0.11 Giga FLOPs, the green bar is at approximately 0.12 Giga FLOPs, and the yellow bar is at approximately 0.10 Giga FLOPs. In Stage 3, the blue bar is at approximately 0.11 Giga FLOPs, the red bar is at approximately 0.10 Giga FLOPs, the green bar is at approximately 0.12 Giga FLOPs, and the yellow bar is at approximately 0.10 Giga FLOPs. The bars are not sorted by height; instead, they are presented in a fixed order corresponding to the legend, which shows blue as the unlabeled baseline, followed by red, yellow, and green. No bars are visually emphasized beyond their color coding and grouping.
